skill.displayName: Amazon 商品详情【Gecho 官方】

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Amazon product-detail workflow that routes user-provided Amazon URLs or ASINs through the Gecho MCP and browser extension setup.

dimensions.detail: The workflow depends on a logged-in Chrome Amazon session and Gecho account, which is sensitive browser-session access, but the dependency is repeatedly disclosed and bounded to product-detail retrieval.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup asks the user to install an external Chrome extension and configure an npx-based Gecho Bridge MCP package, including @latest, but this is disclosed and directly tied to the workflow.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly forbids alternative scraping, browser automation, captcha solving, fabricated data, repeated retries, and operating outside the Gecho MCP workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No artifact-backed persistence, background service installation, privilege escalation, tool hijacking, memory writes, destructive actions, or hidden automatic execution were found in the skill package.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Amazon product detail collection, and the instructions consistently limit execution to the official Gecho amazon_product MCP workflow for user-provided product URLs or ASINs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that this skill requires Gecho Bridge, a Gecho Chrome extension, and a logged-in Amazon browser session. Use it only if you are comfortable letting that external MCP/extension workflow access Amazon product pages visible in your browser session, and review the Gecho package and extension provenance before configuration.
llm.findings: [SQP-3] expected: The SkillSpector concern about Chinese-only instructions is a usability/localization issue rather than a security concern; the artifact is consistently written in Chinese and does not use language choice to hide unrelated authority.
